title: Throughput Chronograph: token cadence microbench for regression-aware TPS
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a tokens-per-second microbenchmark harness ("Chronograph") that exercises core models with realistic cadence profiles and produces stable p95/tokens/sec fingerprints for regression detection. Chronograph should be: reproducible (deterministic workloads + seed control), configurable (sequence lengths, concurrency, KV warmup ratio, batch sizes), CI-friendly (fast smoke runs + nightly full sweep), and integrated with our alerting/bisect pipeline. The goal is to catch subtle TPS regressions and p95 degradations caused by runtime kernel changes, quantization switches, memory layout tweaks, and scheduler tuning. This ticket covers design, implement, dashboarding, and initial CI rollout for 2-3 core model families.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a configurable sweep: concurrency, prompt length distribution, KV warmup fraction, decode length; produces per-run metrics (avg TPS, p50, p95, p99, GPU occupancy, memory pressure)
Nightly CI job executes full Chronograph sweep and writes artifacts to s3://redwood-bench/chronograph/{date}/
Regression detector computes baseline fingerprint and alerts when p95 drops > 10% or avg TPS drops > 12% (configurable thresholds)
Grafana dashboard visualizes trendlines, drift detection signals, and highlights model variant/commit responsible for change
First rollout covers models: rw-7b, rw-chat-13b, and rw-65b-quant; each with separate baseline fingerprints
Integration with bisect automation: when anomaly triggers, create a bisect job ticket with attached artifacts and links to suspect commits
tasks: Design workload generator: mixture of short/medium/long prompts with token cadence profiles
Implement harness runner in python + async request client; reuse perf-connector SDK for endpoint orchestration
Add KV warmup modes (cold, warm, hot) and ensure proper cache priming flows
Instrument telemetry: per-token timing, queueing wait time, kernel handoff markers, GPU SM occupancy metric exports
Store results as JSONL artifacts and push to S3 with stable schema versioning
Create Grafana dashboard + alert rules; wire to CPI (performance-alerts) channel
Add CI jobs: quick smoke (15m) for PRs, nightly full sweep for regression detection
Write runbook: how to interpret chronograph artifacts and trigger bisect
Onboard 3 core models and run baseline collection; commit fingerprints
Doc PRs: Confluence design doc and GH repo README
updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff sync with runtime and infra. Agreed on fingerprint schema and S3 location. Trade-off: longer sweeps give better signal but increase CI cost; decided on fast PR smoke + nightly long sweep.

2025-02-17: Prototype workload generator complete. Uses a weighted sampler for short (8-32 tokens), medium (64-256), and long (512+) contexts. Found that default batcher merges short/long requests and skews measurements; plan to add strict isolation mode for accurate p95 attribution.

2025-02-22: Telemetry schema v1 committed (github.com/redwood-inference/bench/commit/3f2b9a). Telemetry includes per-token delta, server-queue-time, and approximate GPU SM occupancy pulled from nvidia-smi exporter. Noted limitation: occupancy is noisy on shared nodes; will annotate runs with node-labels to filter.
2025-02-26: KV warmup modes implemented. Early runs show ~6% TPS improvement for warm vs cold on rw-chat-13b. Decided to record warmup ratio per-run to aid root cause analysis.

2025-03-01: CI integration spike done. PR smoke job added to circleci (config path .circleci/chronograph-smoke.yml). Smoke runs target a single model and 3 workloads; runtime test took 12m. Nightly job scheduled; still tuning artifact retention policy.

2025-03-04: Initial baseline collection for rw-7b completed. Baseline artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/chronograph/2025-03-04/ENG-314572-rw-7b-baseline.jsonl. Observed p95 = 48.2 tps, avg = 62.5 tps. Added regression threshold at -10% p95.
2025-03-05: Design review with PM and Observability team. Feedback: surface per-route cost breakdown and include model-variant tags (quantized/float16). Added to next sprint tasks.
runbook: How to run locally: 1) checkout github.com/redwood-inference/bench branch chronograph; 2) configure credentials and export REDWOOD_S3_BUCKET; 3) run python -m chronograph.run --model rw-7b --sweep quick --output ./out.jsonl. Interpretation: compare p95 against baseline fingerprint using chronograph/compare.py. If regression detected, capture artifacts and create ENG ticket via /scripts/create_bisect_ticket.sh
